title: Matchbox lifecycle plan approval
description: Authority to apply one specific plan. An approval names the plan by its content hash, so it cannot be reused for different bytes: edit the plan and the approval stops matching. This is attribution, not authentication -- `approved_by` is self-asserted and nothing here proves a human was present. That is deliberate. The property being preserved is that an approval is bound to exactly one reviewed plan; the property a terminal prompt provided, and this does not, is proof of presence.

plan_hash.description: The exact hash of the plan being approved. Compared against the plan's own recomputed hash at apply time, so a hand-edited plan is refused even when its approval is well-formed.

operation.description: The plan's own `operation` value, not a second vocabulary for it. An approval for a `down` plan cannot authorize an `up` plan even in the impossible event of a hash collision, and more usefully, a mismatch catches an approval pointed at the wrong file.

approved_by.description: Who approved this. Self-asserted and recorded verbatim into the receipt.

approved_at.description: RFC3339 timestamp. An input rather than a generated value, so the same review always produces the same artifact.

reason.description: Optional free text. Carried into the receipt unchanged.

authority.description: The record of *how* a mutation was authorized, written into state and into receipts. This definition is the single source of truth for that shape: state.schema.json and receipt.schema.json carry copies, and a test asserts all three are byte-identical, because a contract stated twice is a contract that drifts.

kind.description: `approval` means an artifact named this plan. `terminal` means a controlling terminal was present and the operator confirmed at the prompt. Neither is silently substituted for the other; the receipt says which.
